Akassa Corn Porridge

Served at: Fete du Vodoun (Benin Vodoun Festival)

Serves 4Prep 12 hours (for fermentation)Cook 20 minutes

Akassa is a traditional fermented corn dough porridge commonly enjoyed during the Fete du Vodoun in Benin, a festival celebrating the Vodoun spirit and cultural heritage. This dish is cherished for its tangy flavor and smooth texture, often served alongside spicy sauces or stews to honor the ancestors and spirits during the festivities.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (400 g) cornmeal or fine corn flour
  • 4 cups (960 ml) water
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt

Method

  1. In a large bowl, mix the cornmeal with 2 cups (480 ml) of water to form a smooth batter.
  2. Cover the bowl with a clean cloth and leave it at room temperature to ferment for 12 hours or overnight; the batter should develop a slightly sour aroma.
  3. After fermentation, stir the batter and add the remaining 2 cups (480 ml) of water and salt, mixing well to combine.
  4. Pour the mixture into a medium saucepan and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
  5. Continue stirring and cooking until the porridge thickens to a smooth, creamy consistency, about 15-20 minutes.
  6. Remove from heat and serve warm, traditionally accompanied by spicy sauces or stews during the Fete du Vodoun celebrations.

Tips

  • Use fine cornmeal for a smoother texture; coarser cornmeal will yield a grainier porridge.
  • Fermentation time can vary depending on room temperature; warmer climates speed up fermentation.
  • Serve with traditional Beninese pepper sauce or a vegetable stew for an authentic festival experience.
